note: Faithful rendering of Dharmottara's gloss on the unestablished reason; lemmata and examples correctly segmented.
Difficult kavya verse rendered as prose paragraphs but with the sense of each line preserved; a few obscure lines are reasonably hedged.

errors.english: "What is the nature of destruction?" and so forth is said.
errors.why: The lemma (continuing rgyun from the previous side) is the relative clause 'since [destruction] whose nature is the cutting-off of the continuum...', not a question about the nature of destruction.

fix.find: "What is the nature of destruction?" and so forth is said.
fix.replace: "Since that whose nature is the cutting-off of the continuum..." and so forth:

errors.english: When explaining pots and so forth
errors.why: 'chad par 'gyur ba here is 'to be cut off' (the pot's continuum ceasing), not 'to explain'.

fix.find: When explaining pots and so forth
fix.replace: When a pot and so forth is cut off

errors.english: [note: reincarnation or continuous rebirth of similar moments]
errors.why: mtshams sbyor here is the linking of a similar next moment in an entity's continuum, not reincarnation or rebirth.

note: Argument largely followed, but the opening lemma is turned into a question and 'chad pa is misread as 'explain', obscuring the point about cessation of the continuum.
Bilingual Sanskrit/Tibetan colophon and opening verses of the next avadana rendered accurately, with Sanskrit and Tibetan kept distinct.

errors.english: The text states that the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin) the whole composed of parts produces the cognition.
errors.why: Recognition and the parts produce the cognition OF the whole; the whole is not the producer.

fix.find: The text states that the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin) the whole composed of parts produces the cognition.
fix.replace: That is, recognition and the parts produce the cognition of the "possessor of limbs" (avayavin), the whole composed of parts.

errors.english: because there is no third cognition other than recognition and memory, the objection is raised by the phrase "but if" and so forth.
errors.why: Two separate glosses are merged: 'from that' is explained as 'because there is no third cognition', and then, separately, 'but if' introduces the anticipated objection.

errors.english: the valid means of knowledge would be consistent with the object
errors.why: don dang ldan pa here means the word 'pramana' (in the root text) would be meaningful/purposeful, not that the pramana accords with its object.

errors.english: is a sign established by direct perception
errors.why: The sign is one whose RELATION ('brel pa) is established by perception, and the inference arises from it (completed on the next side); the relation is dropped.

note: The commentary's lemma-and-gloss structure is often blurred and the producer of the cognition of the whole is reversed; usable with real revision.

errors.english: knowingly takes viable, intact seeds from a group of seeds, or seeds that are the abodes of living beings, or those that have not been rendered permissible for mouth consumption,
errors.why: The Tibetan says the monk knows the seeds/abodes are capable of sprouting (khye'u kha 'thon), not made allowable (rung bar ma byas, kalpikrta) and intact; there is no 'taking', no 'mouth consumption', and 'not made allowable' qualifies all, it is not a third category.

fix.find: knowingly takes viable, intact seeds from a group of seeds, or seeds that are the abodes of living beings, or those that have not been rendered permissible for mouth consumption,
fix.replace: knowing that a group of seeds, or seeds that are the abodes of living beings, capable of sprouting and not made allowable, are intact,

note: Accurate Vinaya rendering of the seed categories and offence analysis, except for a misparsed clause in the definition of the actual offence.

errors.english: bring him to mind in the manner in which you have heard of him
errors.why: In the Buddha / (heard teaching) / Sangha sequence, the second object is what one has heard (the Dharma as heard), not the Buddha again; 'him' is supplied by the translator.

note: Clear and faithful rendering of the three kinds of faith and the instruction to the disciple.

errors.english: Heavy materials used for plastering [note: such as dung] should be set on a stone.
errors.why: lci ba is dung (the plastering material), not 'heavy'; gyo mo is a potsherd/tile.

fix.find: Heavy materials used for plastering [note: such as dung] should be set on a stone.
fix.replace: The dung used as material for plastering should be set on a potsherd.

errors.english: did not come until dawn
errors.why: nam sros/srod is nightfall, dusk: he had not come by evening, which is why the pupils then went to bed (he arrives later in the night on the next side).

errors.english: Udāyin made them take him as their preceptor
errors.why: gnas 'char ba is taking dependence (nisraya) on him, i.e. as teacher of dependence, not as preceptor (upadhyaya).

note: Narrative and rules are generally well rendered, but dung read as 'heavy' and dusk as dawn need correction.
Careful rendering of a dense apoha passage, with both summarizing verses kept as verse and the argument structure intact.

errors.english: "Purified" means revealed; the meaning is that it is clearly explained.
errors.why: The lemma, continuing yang from the previous side, is yang dag par ni bstan pa 'it has been correctly shown' (said ironically), not 'purified'.

fix.find: "Purified" means revealed; the meaning is that it is clearly explained.
fix.replace: "[Correctly] shown": the meaning is that it is clearly stated.

errors.english: Whichever sound is depended upon, it is derived from that cause
errors.why: gang gi sgra is 'the word "which"' (yad), and in dependence on it the correlative 'from that cause' is to be supplied; nothing about a sound.

fix.find: Whichever sound is depended upon, it is derived from that cause
fix.replace: In dependence on the word "which," "from that cause" is to be supplied

errors.english: depending on whichever sound, having placed "that cause" in front
errors.why: Again 'the word "which"', not 'whichever sound'.

fix.find: depending on whichever sound, having placed "that cause" in front
fix.replace: depending on the word "which," having placed "that cause" in front

errors.english: because the confusion is identical
errors.why: 'khrul pa here is logical deviation (vyabhicara): the reason deviates equally.

fix.replace: because the deviation is the same

errors.english: this connects to the referent
errors.why: dmigs pa is the verb 'is perceived' (nye bar dmigs so) to which 'from which cause' is construed, not 'the referent'.

errors.english: One must infer this because a definite effect is seen at all times.
errors.why: This sentence is part of the opponent's anticipated objection (introduced by gal te and closed by dogs pa bsu ba), not the commentator's own conclusion.

errors.english: it is not so, thus the objection is raised.
errors.why: The root-text 'No' is introduced to refute the doubt (dogs pa ... 'gog pa, completed on the next side), not to raise an objection.

errors.english: [note: original: "rlung", one of the three humors in Tibetan medicine]
errors.why: The context is the Indian (Ayurvedic) doctrine of the three dosas (vata), not Tibetan medicine.

note: Grammatical lemmata (the word 'which', 'correctly shown') and logical terms are misread and objection/reply segmentation is confused; needs a specialist pass.
